macro_revision_sensitivity.conclusion: Current revised history is not an acceptable substitute for true PIT evidence.

series_attribution.conclusion: Growth is materially more revision-sensitive than Labour.

internal_divergence.conclusion: Internal Growth divergence is a meaningful fragility marker; Labour divergence is mostly a low-conviction marker rather than an additional revision-risk amplifier.

macro_propagation.conclusion: Macro polarity remains stable when underlying block directions remain stable; block-direction revision changes frequently propagate into the Macro state.

turning_point_revision_sensitivity.conclusion: Turning points are materially more timing-sensitive than Macro direction and should be treated as early-warning information rather than structural confirmation.

turning_persistence.conclusion: A single turning point often persists, but immediate structural confirmation is much less frequent.

two_checkpoint_confirmation.conclusion: Persistent turning carries materially more information: about two thirds of these cases are followed by a Macro polarity change within two union-release checkpoints.

research_hierarchy_for_future_evaluation: POSSIBLE_CHANGE: turning persists into the next release checkpoint
CONFIRMED_STRUCTURAL_CHANGE: Macro direction changes with underlying block support
scope_limitations: Evidence is strongest for CAD because CAD is the only G8 currency with full Growth+Labour PIT Macro Core reconstruction.
Do not generalize numeric rates mechanically to other currencies until comparable PIT panels exist.
This gate does not validate Rates, CB/OIS, COT, Liquidity or full 28-pair historical PIT engine behavior.
